scenes.heading: Why a trading journal matters more than a strategy

sents.d: Why a trading journal matters more than a strategy
Tracking decisions reveals patterns a strategy alone can't.

A trading journal — logging entry, exit, reasoning, and emotional state for each trade — often reveals patterns that a strategy alone won't, such as consistently exiting winning trades too early or entering trades out of boredom rather than a real signal.
Reviewing the journal weekly, rather than only after big wins or losses, helps separate genuine strategy problems from emotional decision-making.
Many experienced traders credit journaling, not a specific strategy, as the habit that most improved their consistency over time.

take: Log every trade and your reasoning, and review weekly.
